items.title: 'I Would Stay at That Haunted Inn' — Widow's Bay Cast and Crew Are Just as Attached to the Island as the Rest of Us | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At Apple TV's first ever Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con, the cast and crew of Widow's Bay reacted to the show's breakout success.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic
items.content:
In the middle of a hefty two-hour panel that marked Apple TV's first Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con, the cast and creators of Widow's Bay popped in to reflect on the show's breakout success, which includes 19 recent Emmy nominations. "Dale, I think you had the best reaction," series creator Katie Dippold said to Dale Dickey, who earned one of those Emmy nods for Supporting Actress as Rosemary. "'Dear God in heaven, what the hell just happened,'" Dickey recalled.

Joining Dippold and Dickey on the stage was director Hiro Murai, Stephen Root (Wyck), Jeff Hiller (Dale), K Callan (Ruth), Kevin Carroll (Bashir), and Kingston Rooney Southwick (Evan). (Sadly, no Kate O'Flynn, who plays the fan favorite city hall aide Patricia.)

"It’s amazing it became a watercolor show," Root said, reacting to a question from the moderator, Happy Sad Confused podcast host Josh Horowitz, about the show building up to a zeitgeist-y must-watch. "The tone for he show is everything," he said not long after when they were asked about the series' blend of horror and comedy. "If you get the tone of the show, you’re gonna get the show."

"I feel like every time I did something wrong, they’d say ‘don’t do that,’ and that was a good guardrail," Hiller (half) joked about keeping that sensibility in check.

"I go back to initial conviction — Katie would be like, ‘I know this sounds psychotic, but I would stay at that haunted inn. I would want to get a coffee at that diner," Murai said regarding the grounded feeling of the series despite the terrors of the island. "It should be off-putting to be there, but there’s an inherent coziness. You love this place."

"I would like to be killed there," Dippold said to an appreciative audience.

The cast was asked about each of their characters. Root said that he had "played a lot of heavies" in his life but felt that he could bring "some humanity" to the salty townie Wyck. "You have to see how tirelessly he’s trying to protect the people on the island," he said. "I love being myself a little more in this role than in a lot of other roles I've done. I think it’s about kindness, it really is."

As for Carroll, who plays the exhausted town sheriff whose wife goes into labor during the harrowing season finale, he said the question for his character Bashir is "does he want to be sheriff" of the island? "I think so," Carroll (unexpectedly, to be honest) said. "He's fighting tof his child. What parent in here wou'dnt go to the nth degree for the sake of their children?"

Another major reveal at the end of the first season was an answer to a mystery about how K Callan's Ruth is related to both the founding of the island and Tom and his son Evan. "I knew nothing," Callan said when asked about how clued in she was to Ruth's role. "I got to read the pilot and that was it. I had no idea what Ruth’s journey was going to be. I just put my life in Katie and Hiro’s hand, and thank goodness."

Southwick talked about the importance of the rocky father-son relationship between Evan and Matthew Rhys' Tom. "I think the relationship is so great, because we keep a lot of secrets from each other, and I think that's what kind of keeps us honest," he said. "Certain things that I can do, he can't say that I can't do, because he's doing things that he shouldn't be doing either."

Toward the end of the Widow's Bay time slot, Dickey pulled up a projector screen, recreating a now-iconic scene where Rosemary goes over her geneological findings for the Tom, Patricia, Wyck trio to put an end to the island's bloodlust, that had an old newspaper headline about cannibalism. “It started with cannibalism... right, mayor?" Dickey said, before the screens cut to a live video call from Rhys.

"No, no, you know we don’t talk about cannibalism," joked Rhys, who acknowledged that his mayor is maybe more enthusiastic about managing the island than he is actually proficient at it. "I think his effectiveness would be down to the island to judge," he said. "I think his enthusiasm is without question. He wants the very best for the islandand those who live upon it."

Rhys was also asked about finding the slapstick physicality of his performance as Tom ("I didn’t find anything, Josh, that’s how I live my life") and specifically in Episode 5 as a high-strung, straight-laced goverment leader who happened to take a dose of diabolical-looking mushrooms in Episode 5. "You know, about three to four bottles of good chablis will get you to that place. Which is to be encouraged at times," Rhys said. "It was a lot of fun. YouTube is a great provider these days for acting. I shamelessly copied people enjoying themselves, and that to me was the mushroom trip."

After hanging up with Rhys, Horowitz asked what was most fun to see people obsessing over in the show. "I’m so happy the genealogy scene seemed to land with people," Dippold said about Season 1's penultiamte episode where Rosemary runs down the lengthy ancestry of island founder Richard Warren. "Dale Dickey here memorized that entire thing. I remember the projector screen... I remember it was upside down on the screen so she couldn’t even really use it, she had to to use her mind. Matthew pulled me aside and said, ‘Do you hate Dale Dickey?’"

The Apple TV panel wasn't Widow's Bay's only presence at Comic-Con. At the Showrunners on Showrunning panel Friday afternoon that Dippold participated in alongside Damon Lindelof (Lanterns, Lost) and her former Parks and Recreation boss Greg Daniels (King of the Hill, The Office), the Widow's Bay creator said that she learned the show had been renewed not long before it "became official." She added that the writer's room had started this week and would be active for the next 20 weeks. "The goal is filming early next year."

Other notable reveals from Apple TV's Hall H panel:

Apple TV trotted out a slew of announcements for its first Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday afternoon, including a look at the upcoming second season of Dark Matter, the new Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branaugh movie Mayday, and the back half of SIlo Season 3.

We saw an unexpected release date reveal for its 10-episode Neuromancer series in early 2027. The latest trailer was introduced via video message from its lead Callum Turner, and showunner/executive producer Graham Roland talked about why now was the perfect time to adapt William Gibson's seminal cyperpunk novel.

Hall H got a look at the high-octane trailer for the Matchbox movie (across multiple screens), along with a bit-heavy conversation with the cast where John Cena joked about his fear of doing stunts, which he did for this movie at the request of director Sam Hargrave. "I was scared shitless," told the room. "I like fight choreographym that’s what I feel like I'm fluent at. I hate ledges, I hate heights, I hate cheating death. Each day, I shit my pants. I did a lot of things I'm afraid to do, I conquered none of my fears."

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Project Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

items.title: New Avengers: Doomsday Footage and Poster Revealed at San Diego Comic Con
items.description: Marvel has given fans a new look at Avengers: Doomsday with a fresh poster of Victor Von Doom and an extra clip from the movie showing off his evil abilities.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel has given fans a new look at Avengers: Doomsday with a fresh poster of Victor Von Doom and an extra clip from the movie showing off his evil abilities.

As shown at the Hall H panel on Satuday, July 25, Marvel unveiled a new Doomsday poster showing Doom walking forward, covered in shadows. He looks more menacing than ever, something that holds true to the footage attendees saw that evening.

In an exclusive clip from Doomsday, we see the iconic villain raising up an army of dormant Sentinels - one of the most comic-accurate shots we've had in the MCU.

Doomsday is coming.

Experience Avengers: Doomsday in theaters December 18th. Get tickets now: https://t.co/2HHPv9oLiV pic.twitter.com/WoWRgwW9ut

— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) July 26, 2026

That same clip features a voice over from Sue Storm, saying, "Victor was always the smartest guy. He used to be kind, he used to be caring. Everything he loved was taken from him. He was broken."

Fans were then shown intense shots of Thor, Shang-Chi, Shuri, and Gambit.

Reed Richards says, "Victor, did you do this?"

Doom answers: "All of you... have stolen lives. But now, you must give them back."

Fans were also treated to a humorous clip of Punisher and Spider-Man taking on the Hulk together in Brand New Day, but it's possible that this isn't the Hulk we know and love. Our reporter on the scene described this version of the Hulk as a sort of hybrid between sensible and savage, both angry and growling while also able to hold a coherent conversation in Banner's voice.

This was just one of three big reveals that night; Ryan Gosling was confirmed to play Ghost Rider in a new movie, while Black Panther III was also confirmed, with David Jonsson taking on the mantle.

Doomsday is coming up fast on December 18, 2026, but Black Panther III is slated for a December 15, 2028 release date.

For more Marvel coverage from the weekend, check out our Live Blog, where we published all the news we learned from the Hall H panel as it happened.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Black Panther 3 Release Date Confirmed by Marvel, With David Jonsson Cast as T'Challa's Son | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028.

Details of Ryan Coogler's upcoming threequel were discussed today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance.

Notably, British actor David Jonsson was announced as starring in the film as the son of T'Challa, previously seen as a child in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, who is set to inherit the Black Panther title. Jonsson previously appeared in Alien: Romulus and The Long Walk.

Letitia Wright will return as Shuri, while Winston Duke will reprise his role as M'Baku. So both of them presumably survive Avengers: Secret Wars, then.

For a movie that Marvel had previously not officially confirmed, we actually did know a fair bit about the project before today. Coogler had made no secret of the fact that Denzel Washington is involved after revealing he had written a part specifically for him (and this was back in 2024!). Following this revelation, Kevin Feige then admitted that Black Panther 3 was being planned.

"Denzel is family at this point," Coogler said previously. "I've been trying to work with him since day one. I think he's the greatest living actor. In terms of what he means to our culture? Forget about it, man."

A third entry in the hit MCU Black Panther series had always seemed assured after the first entry hit $1.35 billion and its follow-up Wakanda Forever, which was retooled after the tragic death of original Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman, earned another $859 million.

For all the other news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

Image credit: Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: Deadpool and Peggy Carter Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Ryan Reynolds and Hayley Atwell will reprise their Marvel roles as Deadpool and Peggy Carter in Avengers: Doomsday, it's been confirmed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Ryan Reynolds and Hayley Atwell will reprise their Marvel roles as Deadpool and Peggy Carter in Avengers: Doomsday, it's been confirmed.

Both actors appeared on stage today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. Deadpool now wears a grey suit, which Reynolds referred to as his "Canadian tuxedo."

"Longtime listener, first time caller," Reynolds said, in character as Deadpool, dropping in on the Marvel panel. "I'm a huge fan. I’m not wearing a Doom mask over this mask because I don’t want to ruin the lines of my Canadian tuxedo," he continued, referencing the plastic Doctor Doom masks handed out to everyone in the audience.

Deadpool (or Reynolds?) continued his bit by asking Avengers: Doomsday's directors Joe and Antony Russo when they were beginning to film the movie, so he could drop by and make a cameo. The brothers told Deadpool/Reynolds that the film was already in the can, though they were still tinkering with it.

Jokes aside, it is very safe to say that Deadpool will be in the film, and very likely to assume that Reynolds' scenes were already shot.

For all the news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

items.title: Marvel Announces Ryan Gosling Ghost Rider Movie | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel has announced a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling, directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel has announced a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling, directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy.

First details of the project were confirmed today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. While the film is still a little ways off — it will launch in 2028 — audiences were treated to Gosling and Levy appearing on-stage to discuss the film.

The pair previously worked together filming next year's Star Wars: Starfighter. The fact that Disney is keen for them to re-team again so quickly is likely a promising sign for that film.

The Ghost Rider logo has been revealed at #SDCC, alongside the reveal that Shawn Levy is directing, and it's coming in 2028 pic.twitter.com/L73OqdX51P

— IGN (@IGN) July 26, 2026

Back in March, Ryan Gosling confirmed he'd had discussions with Marvel to play the flame-headed hero Ghost Rider, though said at the time that it was "a complicated situation."

Gosling first mentioned his desire to play Marvel's demonic bike rider back in 2022, which Feige responded positively to at the time. "Hey man, if Ryan wants to be Ghost Rider... Gosling's unbelievable," the Marvel Studios president told MTV News. "Ryan is amazing... I'd love to find a place for him in the MCU."

For all the other news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

items.title: Yaga Trailer Reveals New Series' Horror and Seductive Side
items.author: Jessie Wade
items.content:
The upcoming thriller series Yaga debuted their long-awaited teaser trailer at San Diego Comic-Con during their panel on Saturday, which you can watch below.

The trailer opens with Carrie-Anne Moss (The Matrix) who plays Katherine, a university professor, telling the tale of Baba Yaga to a young playboy-type man, Henry Park, played by Hudson Williams – who looks utterly enthralled by the story.

As the trailer goes on, you see Noah Reid (Schitt's Creek) as Rapp, a private investigator who's trying to solve the disappearance of Henry, and Clark Backo as local detective Carson. More twists seem to come about as things unfold, with Rapp seemingly getting caught up in Baba Yaga's charm and magic, and Henry unleashing intense feelings throughout.

Yaga is based on the play by Kat Sandler, who serves as Showrunner and Executive Producer. The series is a reimagining of the Slavic folktale of Baba Yaga, but is intended to be a darker, sexy, thriller. It's an original series by Canadian streamer Crave, which gained global popularity with Heated Rivarly in late 2025.

Yaga is set to release in October 2026 on AMC+ for US streamers.

Stay tuned to IGN for more reveals from Yaga and the cast at San Diego Comic-Con, and check out everything announced so far at SDCC 2026!

items.title: Exclusive: Coyote vs. Acme Is Getting a Physical Home Media Release with NSFW John Cena Outtakes | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Coyote vs. Acme director Dave Green confirmed to IGN that the film is coming to Blu-ray, along with some hilarious outtakes that he described as “not PG-rated.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Coyote vs. Acme director Dave Green confirmed to IGN that the film is coming to Blu-ray, along with some hilarious outtakes that he described as “not PG-rated.”

We got the chance to chat with Green, as well as Coyote vs. Acme star Lana Condor, at San Diego Comic-Con, where the two gushed about the hilarious moments that happened when John Cena and Will Forte were on set interacting with the Looney Tunes.

“John is an amazing improviser,” Green said. “The camera would keep rolling and he would just love to entertain a room of background actors and make everyone laugh. When you don’t call ‘cut,’ there is minutes and minutes of stuff that is not PG-Rated.”

“Maybe for the Blu-ray,” IGN host Tom Jorgensen replied. “Fingers crossed!”

“I can actually make you that promise,” Green answered. “It’ll be on there.”

In an age where physical media is gradually being phased out in favor of digital downloads, the idea of owning a tangible object that you can play or watch without an internet connection is becoming more and more coveted.

Perhaps the greatest example of this is Sony’s decision to stop printing physical game discs starting January 2028 — a choice that has left the gaming community in disarray, scrambling to get their hands on PlayStation’s final physical releases before the cutoff date.

While some big releases are confirmed for a full physical release, others, like the highly anticipated GTA 6, will have a digital download only (though you can still buy the box that the code comes in, if that counts).

Coyote vs. Acme releases in theaters on August 28, 2026 — a welcome development after it was notably shelved by Warner Bros. Discovery in 2023 for a $30 billion tax write-off. Now audiences can see the movie in its entirety, along with a few R-rated special features when it comes to Blu-ray.

items.title: Rockstar Co-Founder Says 'if People Want' Physical Game Releases Then 'Companies Should Provide It'
items.description: Rockstar Games co-founder Dan Houser believes that, if players want their games released on physical media, then "companies should provide it."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Rockstar Games co-founder Dan Houser believes that, if players want their games released on physical media, then "companies should provide it."

The former Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption developer opened up about the state of physical media in the gaming space during a conversation with IGN at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. He didn't have a strong opinion when asked if he personally cares about physical versus digital releases, but when it comes to others, his thoughts were pretty cut and dry.

"I don't know that I care, but if people want that, I think companies should provide it," Houser said. "But I don't know that I personally care.

"I also think that, as critical as people are of digital releases, the ability to update and fix problems in games has been really useful for the quality of games."

The question arrives as gamers of every background take to social media to sound off about recent changes in the physical and digital gaming space. PlayStation has found itself in headlines for weeks after confirming it would cease production of new physical games starting in January 2028. Funnily enough, Rockstar has also been involved in the conversation, with Grand Theft Auto fans still coming to terms with confirmation that GTA 6 will not ship on a disc when it launches this November.

Lazlow Jones, who worked with Houser at Rockstar before leaving to join him at Absurd Ventures, was also in attendance at SDCC. In his response to the question, he explained his relationship with both physical and digital games.

"We all have that sort of feeling when you get that copy, and you put the disc in the console, but I also have to say I really like being at the airport and going, 'Oh, cool. I can download some quick games to my Steam Deck for this 12-hour flight.'

"That's what's been interesting. We've worked in digital together for a lot of years, and then making a physical product of a comic book is a different creative process but also just really fulfilling to have a physical thing you can say, 'Look. We made a thing.'"

Houser interjected: "I love physical media."

The Rockstar co-founder isn't the first developer to share his thoughts about the state of physical media. Nier creator Yoko Taro, Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima, and Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot are just a few of the names who have chimed in with thoughts recently.

For now, Houser is at Absurd Ventures, a company he founded and officially announced in 2023. For more on his thoughts on the industry, you can see what he had to say about how people play open-world games.

Photo by Chelsea Guglielmino/Getty Images.

items.title: Neuromancer Release Date, First Look Revealed for Apple TV | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly-anticipated cyberpunk series.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly anticipated cyberpunk series.

As revealed during the Apple TV panel in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Neuromancer will come to the streaming service on Friday, January 22, 2027.

Showrunner and executive producer Graham Roland gave fans a few more details on what they can expect from the first-ever screen adaptation of William Gibson's genre-defining novel, explaining why now is the perfect time to bring it to life.

"42 years ago, this book felt like true science fiction," Roland said. "Gibson famously coined the term 'cyberspace' to describe a digital space where people in the book go to to escape and interact [with each other], and he did all that before the internet existed.

"He wrote about the collision of artificial intelligence and human intelligence before artificial intelligence existed. Now, we’re living in a world 40 years later where these things are a part of our everyday lives. It's an appropriate time to revisit the text, to put it in a new light now that these things are here."

Roland also shed some light on what it's been like working with Callum Turner, who plays the book's central character and resident console cowboy, Case. Notably, Roland said that Turner has a big love for Neuromancer, and confirmed that this series is focused on Case.

"He wrote about the collision of artificial intelligence and human intelligence before artificial intelligence existed. Now, we're living in a world where these things are part of our everyday lives."

"Everyone came with a deep love of the source material," he said. "He read the book, dove into his character. Case is an atypical protagonist. He's a criminal, rough around the edges, he’s a survivor. In the book, there's no mention of his family, he’s kind of an orphan, doing out of an instinct of survival, desperation. Callum threads that needle. He's able to play the dangerous part of Case, inhabit the humanity and charisma. One of the things that's very important is that this is Case’s story, you’re following him. The charisma needs to carry you for 10 episodes."

While Turner wasn't physically present at the Comic-Con panel, he did send a video message, which glitched out and eventually lead to a teaser of the show.

"We're building something special with Neuromancer," Turner said. "[Gibson] didn’t just give us cyberspace, he helped us define the entire cyperpunk genre. This is just your first access point."

"The future is in your mind."

Check out the official teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/gOqHiavOpv

— IGN (@IGN) July 25, 2026

The trailer, which is now live on YouTube, shows a good look at Briana Middleton as Molly with her mirror eyes and deadly fingernails that earn her the moniker 'razorgirl,' the cyberpunk setting of the story, and, of course, Mark Strong as Armitage. It's dark, gritty, and intense.

This is the latest big reveal for Neuromancer after Apple TV+ shared a first look at the series with a 25-second clip two weeks ago. In the clip, someone (presumably Case) pushes a button on a retro computer console. The camera then pans up to a TV screen, which displays the words 'Ashpool-1' and the opening line of Gibson's novel: "The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel."

Gibson himself is executive producer of the show alongside Roland, JD Dillard, and Jennifer Haley. Dillard directed the first three episodes of the series, two of which will premier on Apple TV starting January 22, 2027. Episodes drop weekly on Friday through March 19, 2027. There are ten episodes in all.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Dungeons & Dragons Movie Sequel Has a Script But 'Financial Reasons' Might Keep It from Ever Coming Out
items.description: Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves co-director Jonathan Goldstein says the script for a sequel already exists, but he's not expecting it to see the light of day any time soon.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves co-director Jonathan Goldstein says the script for a sequel already exists, but he's not expecting it to see the light of day any time soon.

The filmmaker behind the 2023 D&D adaptation gave fans an unfortunate update when speaking with ScreenRant at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. Fans praised the original movie for how it faithfully brought the classic tabletop roleplaying game to the big screen, but it doesn't sound like its favorable reception from critics and audiences will do much to bring a sequel to life.

"We actually wrote a sequel to Dungeons and Dragons," Goldstein said. "We were hired to write it. I don't know that it will see the light of day for a number of financial reasons. They're expensive movies to make, but it'd be great fun to do it. We love that cast, and we think we wrote something that fans would like."

Those "financial reasons" he mentioned are probably a reference to Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves' box office returns. Despite rolling into its opening weekend as the number one movie in theaters domestically, its final global total saw it bring in just $205.46 million (via Box Office Mojo). It’s a respectable enough finish on its own, but considering Variety reported the film cost $150 million before factoring in marketing costs, things could have gone much, much better for the D&D movie.

Still, the fact a sequel script was written suggests someone at Paramount was interested in keeping the story going at some point. The original film – which starred Chris Pine (Edgin), Michelle Rodriguez (Holga), Justice Smith (Simon), Sophia Lillis (Doric), Hugh Grant (Forge), and Regé-Jean Page (Xenk) – has certainly managed to garner a group of die-hard fans since its premiere.

Its Rotten Tomatoes scores, for example, sit at 91% from critics and 92% from fans. IGN gave the film a 7/10 review, calling it an "accessible fantasy adventure that both roasts and respects D&D culture without losing newcomers along for the ride."

With a script on the table and Paramount going through its own changes every day, it's unclear if Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves sequel will ever come to be. Former Paramount Pictures CEO Brian Robbins had previously stated he would be interested in doing a second movie, but only if it could be made "for less." Pine, meanwhile, said in 2023 that he was "pretty confident" it would happen eventually.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.title: The Most Anticipated Warhammer 40,000 Animation Ever Finally Has a Release Date
items.description: Games Workshop has finally given Warhammer 40,000 fans the news they’ve craved for years: a release date for animated series Astartes 2.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Games Workshop has finally given Warhammer 40,000 fans the news they’ve craved for years: a release date for animated series Astartes 2.

In a post on Warhammer Community, Games Workshop said Astartes 2 is set to drop this December. Via a new promo video, we also have two new shots of Astartes 2, which you can see in the slideshow below. Don't expect a huge amount from the images though, they don't give away much. And there's still much we don't know about Astartes 2 itself. How many episodes will it be? How long will the episodes be? Will it even be divided up into episodes this time?

For the uninitiated, the original Astartes was created by superfan Syama Pedersen, who was subsequently brought into the fold to make the official sequel. In November last year, Games Workshop revealed animation work on a monitor screen via the promo video below, showing a squad of Terminators appearing to protect an unnamed human soldier. This is the Inquisition-led Deathwatch Terminator squad from the debut Astartes 2 teaser in incomplete form, but we know from their pauldron chapter symbols that they’re the same as before (Retributors, Mortifactors, Scythes of The Emperor, Sons of Medusa, and Angels Vermilion).

Astartes is widely accepted as the greatest Warhammer 40,000 animation ever made, official or unofficial, with only Amazon’s excellent Space Marine 2 animation for the Secret Level anthology series competing with it in quality terms. Indeed, Astartes was so good that it inspired Saber Interactive’s hugely successful Space Marine 2 in terms of the look and feel of the Space Marines themselves.

Fans hadn’t heard a peep out of Games Workshop on Astartes 2 for years, leading some to wonder whether the company had quietly cancelled it. But in January last year Games Workshop released a teaser trailer alongside a 2026 release window, and now we know it will be out this December. GW managed to get it in before the end of the year just in time!

Last year’s teaser suggested an animation on a scale and quality never-before-seen from Warhammer 40,000, with melee combat, shooting, vehicle combat, and even spaceship battles all showcased. It showed a number of Space Marine chapters in battle across varied environments, and multiple enemy races, including Tyranids, Orks, and Tau.

But it turned out that nothing in the teaser is actually in the Astartes 2 animation itself. According to a post on the Warhammer Community website: “This teaser trailer is not actually clips from the new animation, instead showing a compilation of shots that represent the former lives of the characters that will appear in the show. There’s a pretty unsubtle hint at the end as to the nature of the final story... We’ll leave you to speculate and start putting the pieces together yourselves.”

Astartes 2 will be available via Games Workshop's streaming service, Warhammer TV.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: George R.R. Martin Working on Dunk and Egg Book Four, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Showrunner Says
items.description: Game of Thrones mastermind and A Song of Ice and Fire author George R.R. Martin is working on a fourth Dunk and Egg book, according to A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms showrunner Ira Parker.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Game of Thrones mastermind and A Song of Ice and Fire author George R.R. Martin is working on a fourth Dunk and Egg book, according to A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms showrunner Ira Parker.

The HBO showrunner opened up about the future of the fantasy spinoff during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. While his adaptation of Martin's Dunk and Egg stories has only received a green light for up to Season 2, he's stated in the past that he'd love to expand this live-action version of the tales of Ser Duncan the Tall (Peter Claffey) and Egg (Dexter Sol Ansell).

If all goes well, he's hoping to expand into three seasons "or maybe four or five." Part of what might help A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms move forward is if Martin can finish the next Dunk and Egg chapter on time.

"Book four, which George is working on, takes place in a very cool location," Parker teased. "And five is the last story point of Egg as a boy. So it’s a very natural ending place for us to take a break and come back when Dexter is older. So then we can do Egg the Prince, do some politics, do some fun stuff in Summer Hall and King’s Landing, and get a different vibe where they’re not on the road all the time."

Martin has previously expressed his interest in continuing the Dunk and Egg series of novellas. For now, however, that wing of the Game of Thrones universe is limited to The Hedge Knight, The Sworn Sword, and The Mystery Knight. According to Parker, Martin is hoping to make that change, though he failed to elaborate on that "very cool location."

Meanwhile, Martin has, of course, been infamously reluctant to publish the penultimate installment in his A Song of Ice and Fire series, The Winds of Winter. Although he's not thrilled how long it's taken either, the 77-year-old author doesn't exactly have a backup plan if he's unable to finish it before he dies. Where this alleged fourth Dunk and Egg novella falls on the ever-expanding release timeline remains a mystery.

As for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Parker had expressed interest in taking a break between later seasons to allow the actors to age accordingly. It's an idea that HBO executives have mostly given him "eye rolls" over, though it sounds like they're "not completely" turned off by it.

"So if the show wraps and people are still OK with everything we’re doing and there’s still an appetite," Parker continued, "let the show evolve along with our leads, with myself and with the rest of our creative team as we grow older and the world changes and we want to say different things. I think that would be a lovely way to tell a story about these two guys through the course of their lives."

Parker previously stated that, while he doesn't believe A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms seasons will outpace Martin's work, the author has at least provided the HBO team with 12 outlines for future stories. Although these were described as a rough look at the road ahead, it sounds like the Dunk and Egg show could continue for a while longer, should enough viewers ask for it.

Parker also teased that he and the team have laid eyes on some of Martin's unpublished work.

"He gave me some unpublished pages — actual written prose he found in his files somewhere that he sent over, and we used them," he added.

While we wait for more Dunk and Egg and continue waiting for The Winds of Winter, you can see what IGN thought of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Season 1 in our 8/10 review. You can also check out the latest update on Season 2.

Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images.

items.title: DC's Next Level Initiative Expands, Including a Must-Read Batman Comic | Comic Con 2026
items.description: DC revealed an enticing lineup of books at Comic-Con, including a new Batman series from the minds behind Absolute Martian Manhunter.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
DC's Next Level initiative has been a big success for the company over the past year, and they're looking to continue that momentum into 2027. The publisher revealed a new wave of Next Level titles at Comic-Con, including a very intriguing new Batman comic from the minds behind the Eisner-winning series Absolute Martian Manhunter.

The Batman series in question is a new volume of Shadow of the Bat, written by Deniz Camp and drawn by Javier Rodríguez. Camp teased at SDCC that the series is very much about confronting the failure of Gotham's institutions and reinventing Batman for the current moment. Fans of Camp's The Ultimates run (which won IGN's Best Comic Book Series of 2024 award) should be in for a treat.

Also on the Batman front, DC is releasing a star-studded one-shot special as part of Batman Day in September. Batman of Two Worlds features two interconnected tales, one focused on the classic Dark Knight by Batman writer Matt Fraction and DC K.O. artist Javi Fernández, and the other on Absolute Batman from writer Scott Snyder and Doom Patrol artist Nick Derington.

“You have two different looks at Batman,” said Fraction in a statement. “The moral structures, the ethical structures, the political structures. A chance to put them side by side and see the similarities and differences.”

Outside of Batman, Exquisite Corpses creator Michael Walsh is writing and drawing a new six-issue series called Jonah Hex and the Shadow of Death. DC's official description teases:

Welcome to the end of the Wild West. Welcome to the quiet life of a broken-down bounty hunter whose own story, one of bloodshed, pain, and guilt, ended long ago—or so he thought.
In a small town called Ashecott, something evil has arrived. Something more dangerous than a gunslinger, more sinister than an outlaw, and older than the town it seeks to infect. Something from a world beyond the only one its victims have ever known. Something darker.
Unfortunately for that evil, Jonah Hex has taken notice. Not just of the otherworldly entities surrounding his home, or the child with mysterious abilities they seek to capture—but also of the chance to finally redeem himself.
Join master of horror Michael Walsh as he begins a terrifying new era of DC’s haunted bounty hunter!

Then, Ultramega creator James Harren is tackling a new take on an old favorite with The Demon. DC's description teases:

The world is infested with a darkness its people cannot see. Beasts from Hell feast on humanity’s soul, sucking it dry and leaving nothing but a shell behind.
Only one person can see these monsters and cast them back to Hell: Jason Blood! But he is a shadow of the man he once was, wandering the world following the face of a wizard long gone and hearing a voice in his head demanding to be let out.
How can Jason Blood help protect the world from demons when he himself is not sure how to work with the one bound to his soul? Will the Demon Etrigan ever rise again?
Superstar writer/artist James Harren (Ultramega) creates a brand-new epic starring the mightiest demon of them all!

Finally, fans can also look forward to a new Static series by Cody Ziglar and Diego Olortegui and a new Vixen series by Stephanie Williams and Khary Randolph.

In other DC-related Comic-Con news, we think we know the real villain of the Lanterns TV series, and Amazon has revealed an exclusive Batman: Caped Crusader video game.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

items.content:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has acknowledged the "open world fatigue" affecting the industry but says Square Enix was "very careful" to make sure fans would have "all the guidance they need" in the new remake chapter – even if it's bigger than the last.

The developer helping lead the finale to its 2027 launch spoke about its size during a conversation with Eurogamer. In the interview, he teased how the team has done its best to tie a bow on the trilogy with one final adventure for Cloud, Tifa, Barret, and the rest of the gang in their fight against Sephiroth.

The two previous installments in the remake trilogy – Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth – have been lumped into online conversations about enormous open worlds that sometimes overstay their welcome. Hamaguchi said the concept of open world fatigue is "very important" to him, but it sounds like players won't need to worry about feeling too lost.

"There are a lot of open world games out in the world right now, and [the idea of 'open world fatigue'] is a very important concept to me," he replied when Eurogamer asked about feedback to Rebirth. "It depends on personal preference and different perceptions, but for me personally, I know I've had the experience where I've been thrown out into an open world game and not known where to go, not known where to begin, and not known what to do. But at the same time, the concept of being thrown into this wondrous world where anything goes is amazing."

There are certainly players who would prefer to get lost in a vibrant fantasy universe. In a world promising to be as packed as Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, that idea might be especially enticing. Hamaguchi said that, as a creator, he believes it's important to "offer proper guidance" in open-world games so that players "know what to do, and know where to go."

"In Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, we made sure to make it easy for the players to understand how much content there is, and how difficult that content is," he added. "That design philosophy is applied to Revelation: players have all the guidance that they need. This is something that both myself and the development team were very careful about when we designed the game."

It seems Hamaguchi and the rest of the development team wanted to strike a balance when it came to guidance in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. One example he mentioned involved asking players to rely on their memory to make sure they land in their desired location when dropping from the Highwind airship.

"That's another example of the guidance we're giving players, without directing them too much," Hamaguchi continued. "The world is even bigger than it was in Rebirth, so it is more important than ever for us to ensure there's enough guidance here, so people have no issues enjoying what this game has to offer."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation currently has no firm release date but is expected to launch for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S in spring 2027. While we wait for updates, you can read about what Hamaguchi had to say about the feedback to Remake and Rebirth's vast pool of mini-games. You can also learn about the leak that suggests DLC may be in development.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Sets Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date for Early August
items.description: Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy 14 has a Nintendo Switch 2 release date of August 4, 2026.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy 14 has a Nintendo Switch 2 release date of August 4, 2026.

Game director Naoki Yoshida (a.k.a. Yoshi-P) suited up in Bastion armor and took the stage at Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin to confirm the news alongside a laundry list of new updates coming in the near future. While Square Enix had previously confirmed plans to bring FFXIV to Switch 2 in August, today's news locks in a launch that's only a little more than one week away.

Preorders begin later today, with fans told to keep an eye on Square Enix social media for updates. When FFXIV goes on sale August 4, its first month of sale will be free of subscription charges as the developers ensure server stability. After this period comes to an end, players will be required to purchase a subscription as normal.

"We knew that you've been waiting for this for a long time," Yoshi-P said via translator, "so we're very happy to bring this to you."

Final Fantasy 14 Fan Fest 2026 also allowed Yoshi-P to go back over some of the catches that come with the Switch 2 version of the game. As revealed at Anaheim Fan Fest in April, FFXIV for Nintendo fans will require a separate subscription.

Yoshi-P said at the time that the decision to require an individual subscription on Switch 2 came after "many months of discussions with Nintendo," but it's not all bad news. A Nintendo Switch Online subscription won't be required to play, for example. Additionally, those who have active FFXIV subscriptions elsewhere can take advantage of a 50% discount on Switch 2.

FFXIV is only days away from its Switch 2 launch. Also revealed during the presentation was more information on the upcoming Evercold expansion, the Bastion tank role, a new Final Fantasy 7 collaboration, and more.

For more, you can read IGN's original 8.6/10 review. You can also read about how the game rewards Japanese players for paying their real-life taxes.

items.title: Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter Win Big at the 2026 Eisner Awards | Comic Con 2026
items.description: DC's Absolute Universe dominated the 2026 Eisner Awards, with both Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter taking home key trophies.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
The winners of the the 2026 Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards were revealed at San Diego Comic-Con. DC took home some major awards on the strength of its Absolute Universe line, with both Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter being honored. In total, DC was the most decorated publisher with 10 awards (including Best Continuing Series, Best Limited Series, and Best One-Shot/Single Issue), followed by Image Comics with four awards.

items.title: Spaceballs: The New One Creators on Making Mel Brooks' Yogurt CGI and Paying Tribute to John Candy | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Rick Moranis appeared at SDCC alongside Josh Gad to reveal new details for Spaceballs: The New One, including Mel Brooks' now CGI Yogurt and fresh Star Wars gags.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
The Schwartz was stronger than ever in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con. A packed room of thousands of fans cheering on the panel for a sequel nearly 40 years in the making, Spaceballs: The New One.

Rick Moranis' presence was an understandable major deal for the audience, with the comedy legend making his long-awaited return to the screen as he reprises his role as the villain Dark Helmet. Moderator Kevin Smith introduced Moranis with what turned into an elaborate bit where he failed to walk on stage, only for some costumed Spaceball soldiers "combing the crowd" (giant comb included, naturally) to find him. When Moranis actually did take the stage, he got a massive standing ovation.

Not there in person was another legend, original Spaceballs writer and director Mel Brooks, with the 100 year old (!) sending a very funny video, in which he cracked jokes like, “Sorry I can’t be there! I’m on convention floor trying to buy a rare Charizard card!” and "When I was your age, on a Friday, I’d go to something called 'work.'"

Brooks' age came up when discussing him reprising his role as Yogurt. In the original film, Brooks wore elaborate makeup, but Brooks told director Josh Greenbaum and writers Josh Gad (who also produced), Dan Hernandez and Benji Samit that while he was excited to participate, he couldn't do the makeup anymore. Instead, Yogurt will now be a digital character, with Brooks providing the voice. Greenbaum laughed about how Brooks had dots on his face at his first voice recording sessions for the mocap team to use as reference points, only for Brooks to declare "I don’t need the dots.” Greenbaum got the OK from the VFX supervisors to proceed without them.

It was Gad who got the ball rolling on Spaceballs returning inspired to do so after he and Moranis were going to make a Honey, I Shrunk the Kids follow-up that never came to be. He pitched his idea to Brooks, who was excited by it. Gad said he felt the time was right for a Spaceballs sequel because it can comment on how we are living in an age of nostalgia and how there is now so much more Star Wars to parody when the first Spaceballs only had the original trilogy as its basis.

Gad apologized that even though this is a parody of Star Wars, they still were keeping actual secrets like a Star Wars movie, including details on new characters played by Keke Palmer and Gad (though Lewis Pullman is confirmed to play Starburst, the son of Bill Pullman's Lone Star and Daphne Zuniga's Queen Vespa). Gad said he wanted Spaceballs: The New One to be a love letter to someone who sat alongside Moranis on Gad's personal comedy Mount Rushmore, the late John Candy. Gad stressed he was not playing Candy's character, Barf, but is playing another Mawg, Barf's alien species. Gad also promised an that there will be an acknowledgement in the film to other original Spaceballs cast members who have passed away, including Joan Rivers, Dick Van Patten and Dom DeLuise.

The panel ended with a montage of footage from the film that was a slightly re-edited version of the footage first shown at the Amazon AMC CinemaCon panel in April. Some of the gags from that earlier version — such as a Harry Potter parody moment — were removed, but there were also new bits, like Dark Helmet proclaiming "Somehow I've returned... somehow!" We also see a Doctor Strange-style portal open, glimpses of Palmer's character Destiny sporting a decidedly Rey-influenced look, and many other rapid-fire gags, including Yogurt getting hit by a freeze blast and someone proclaiming, "Frozen Yogurt!" It was all backed by a choir singing the Spaceballs theme song from the original film.

The Spaceballs panel was also notable for being one of the rare Hall H panels to use the special side screens, usually saved for would-be epic event movies that want to make a visual impact. This made it all the funnier when the filmmakers did a mock Spaceballs Cinematic Universe slate reveal that included dozens of titles that spanned 11 phases with titles like 2 Space 2 Balls, Pizza the Hutt: Cheesy Does It, Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs, The Space and The Balls, Spaceballs: The Lawsuit, Spaceballs: Enough is Enough, and Spaceballs: Enough is Never Enough.

Moranis said it was the right time for him to return in Spaceballs: The New One, noting he had a terrific time making it. "I was in that outfit and I was in the helmet and it felt really strange and it started to feel really good and I started to love it," he said about being on set again. "And who knows? Maybe it’s the beginning of many." (Just probably not 11 phases worth...)

The panel ended with a montage of footage from the film that was a slightly re-edited version of the footage first shown at the Amazon AMC CinemaCon panel in April. Some of the gags from that earlier version — such as a Harry Potter parody moment — were removed, but there were also new bits, like Dark Helmet proclaiming "Somehow I've returned... somehow!" We also see a Doctor Strange-style portal open, glimpses of Palmer's character Destiny sporting a decidedly Rey-influenced look, and many other rapid-fire gags, including Yogurt getting hit by a freeze blast and someone proclaiming, "Frozen Yogurt!" It was all backed by a choir singing the Spaceballs theme song from the original film.

The Spaceballs panel was also notable for being one of the rare Hall H panels to use the special side screens, usually saved for would-be epic event movies that want to make a visual impact. This made it all the funnier when the filmmakers did a mock Spaceballs Cinematic Universe slate reveal that included dozens of titles that spanned 11 phases with titles like 2 Space 2 Balls, Pizza the Hutt: Cheesy Does It, Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs, The Space and The Balls, Spaceballs: The Lawsuit, Spaceballs: Enough is Enough, and Spaceballs: Enough is Never Enough.

Moranis said it was the right time for him to return in Spaceballs: The New One, noting he had a terrific time making it. "I was in that outfit and I was in the helmet and it felt really strange and it started to feel really good and I started to love it," he said about being on set again. "And who knows? Maybe it’s the beginning of many." (Just probably not 11 phases worth...)

items.description: God of War Laufey has a release date: February 16, 2027.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
God of War Laufey has a release date: February 16, 2027.

Confirmation comes from the God of War Laufey panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, which IGN attended. A 2027 release date was expected for God of War Laufey after Sony Santa Monica confirmed it would ship on-disc. The announcement came after Sony said it would stop production of PlayStation discs from 2028, sparking a backlash.

At the same panel, Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey, and connects directly to her story.

Early reaction to God of War Laufey has been mixed, with some fans praising the game's combat and visuals, while others have criticized the simplistic gameplay seen in Laufey's opening section — and, predictably, the fact that fan-favorite Kratos wasn't center stage. (We’ve got an explainer on Faye herself for more on her story.)

Our first glimpse at God of War Laufey, seen in a 20-minute gameplay segment aired at the end of June's PlayStation State of Play showcase, began with Kratos and Atreus burning Faye's body — as seen in 2018's God of War. Kratos then pops up again shortly after, aiding Faye while she's briefly imprisoned. It remains unclear if Kratos will make any other appearances before Laufey's credits roll, or if these brief glimpses of the hero are it, as he's then busy with the events of God of War Ragnarök.

items.title: Next Kratos-Led God of War Game Is Coming After Laufey, and Connects Directly to Her Story | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog has announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey, and connects directly to her story.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog has announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey, and connects directly to her story.

Confirmation comes from the God of War Laufey panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, which IGN reported on live here.

No further details were offered at the panel, although God of War Laufey now has a confirmed release date of February 16, 2027. We have no indication yet when this Kratos-led God of War game will come out, or which platform it is targeting. Nor do we have confirmation of its title or its setting.

During the panel, Barlog said of God of War Laufey that he wanted to see an extension and expansion of the world where the characters we meet are unexpected. "Everything we are doing in the Faye game is a continuation of what came before and to set up and expand what comes next," he explained. "Phranque has been around since the beginning. It's interesting to see how to build this world out. Everything in the game is setting up for something so amazing."

In June, following the reveal of the Faye-starring next chapter of God of War, Santa Monica Studio discussed Kratos' future as the figurehead of its flagship franchise. Speaking in an interview uploaded to PlayStation's YouTube channel, Barlog said that "there's always going to be Kratos games" — a position backed up by a later post from the company's official social media account, which stated that the studio had "many more stories to tell with him."

Early reaction to God of War Laufey has been mixed, with some fans praising the game's combat and visuals, while others have criticized the simplistic gameplay seen in Laufey's opening section — and, predictably, the fact that fan-favorite Kratos wasn't center stage. (For a full catch-up, we’ve got an explainer on Faye herself for more on her story.)

"Faye is, while it's a different thing, it's still part of the larger tapestry of what we truly really want to explore, all of these different characters in there," Barlog said of the new game. "But there's always going to be Kratos games, like, throughout the whole history. We're super excited about that."

"Oh for sure," added Lawrence. "We can't not tell stories about the big guy."

Our first glimpse at God of War Laufey, seen in a 20-minute gameplay segment aired at the end of June's PlayStation State of Play showcase, began with Kratos and Atreus burning Faye's body — as seen in 2018's God of War. Kratos then pops up again shortly after, aiding Faye while she's briefly imprisoned. It remains unclear if Kratos will make any other appearances before Laufey's credits roll, or if these brief glimpses of the hero are it, as he's then busy with the events of God of War Ragnarök.

"Kratos is the God of War – we have many more stories to tell with him," Santa Monica Studio's official X/Twitter account wrote in a post. "For now, we're excited to take fans on a journey into the afterlife of the gods with Faye and hope you’ll come along for the ride!"

Of course, Santa Monica Studio has also announced a remake of the God of War Greek trilogy remake — which will see Kratos back in the spotlight. The original God of War launched back in 2005 for PS2, with its sequel arriving two years later. God of War 3, for PS3, then debuted in 2010. No release date for the God of War Trilogy Remake was announced, and work is still in its "early stages."
